history.period: Late 16th century, Mughal era (reign of Akbar) - legendary
history.summary: Temple tradition says Raja Mansingh of Amber found a shivalinga on Attock hill during an Afghan campaign under Akbar, brought it to Agra and installed it here; Rawal Rajputs living around the shrine gave it the name Rawali (Rawali Mahadev). The temple stands on Mahatma Gandhi Road, Rakabgunj, Agra, and local lore says the British-era railway line had to be diverted around it rather than moved. It also houses idols of Bajrang Bali, Ram, Radha-Krishna and Bhairon Baba and follows a mahant tradition. History is temple legend reported by MyAdhyatm, not documented (verify).

town_description: Agra is a historic city in western Uttar Pradesh on the Yamuna, once the capital of the Mughal Empire; it is world-famous for the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, and its old city holds many older local shrines alongside the Mughal monuments.
